text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner and former Preussag Stahl AG chairman Kurt Staehler have agreed to moderate talks between Thyssen AG and Krupp about a possible merger of their steel operations, a state government official said on Thursday.

The talks, which begin on Thursday, offer a chance to reach a long-term viable plan for the steel industry in North Rhine-Westphalia, centre of both the German steel and coal industries, state economics minister Wolfgang Clement said, according to the prepared text of a speech.
"It is now clear that we stand before far-reaching changes in the steel sector," Clement said. Rationalisation means investment for innovation and modernisation, but also job cuts, he said.
"Let no one be fooled. The alternative to a crash course, a joint steel company, will not only secure jobs, it will cost jobs," he said.
Talks about a merged steel company have arisen periodically for many years, always without success. "Now there is a chance to realise together a long-term, viable concept," he said.
There can be no political guarantee for the jobs in the steel sector, but the state is counting on cooperation rather than confrontation among the parties, he said.
Steel is a high-technology industry that can remain competitive in North Rhine-Westphalia, he said.
The state, once Germany's industrial heartland, has already moved far to restructure its economy.
